title: 1:1 & Mentoring
description: Feedback, career talk, and coaching phrases.

items.scenario: In a 1:1, your report seems quiet and overloaded.

choices.text: Why is your output low?
I want to check in on workload and energy. What feels heaviest right now, and what would make the next two weeks more sustainable?
Fill the whole 1:1 with your status monologue.
Skip 1:1s when people look fine.

items.explanation: Open with care and a concrete sustainability ask.

items.scenario: You need to give hard feedback about missed stakeholder updates.

choices.text: You are bad at communication.

In the last two incidents, stakeholders learned status late. The impact was avoidable escalations. Going forward I need a status note within 15 minutes of SEV start. Let's practice a template together today.
Put it only in the annual review surprise.
Hint vaguely and hope they notice.

items.explanation: Behavior + impact + clear future standard + support.

items.scenario: Report asks how to grow toward staff/SRE leadership.

choices.text: Just work harder.
For the next quarter, let's target two outcomes: leading one cross-team reliability initiative and mentoring an on-call buddy. We will review evidence monthly against those outcomes.
Titles are meaningless; never plan.
Promise a promotion date with no criteria.

items.explanation: Growth plans need outcomes, evidence, and review cadence.

items.scenario: As a report, you want more challenging work.
items.prompt: How do you ask your manager?

choices.text: I am bored; this job is easy.
I am ready for more ownership. Could I lead the next canary rollout with your sponsorship? I will draft a plan this week and identify risks I still need help with.
Threaten to leave immediately.
Wait silently for someone to notice.

items.explanation: Ask for ownership with a plan and explicit sponsorship needs.

items.scenario: Performance is slipping due to unclear priorities across teams.

choices.text: Try harder to please everyone.
Your priorities are split across three stakeholders. Together we will define a ranked top three for this sprint, and I will reinforce that order with the other managers.
Blame the employee only.
Add more meetings.

items.explanation: Managers remove ambiguity and shield priority order.

items.scenario: Report made a production mistake and feels ashamed.

choices.text: You should feel bad.

Thank you for owning it quickly. Mistakes happen in complex systems. Let's focus on the learning and the preventive change. I still trust you on-call — we will pair on the first shift back if you want.
Remove them from on-call forever immediately.
Joke about it in public Slack.

items.scenario: You disagree with your manager's technical direction.

choices.text: That plan is dumb.
I see the goal. My concern is blast radius without canaries. Can we walk through a safer sequence that still hits the date, or explicitly accept the risk if we skip it?
Complain to the team after the 1:1.
Sabotage the plan quietly.

items.explanation: Challenge with risk, alternative, and decision clarity.

items.scenario: Mentoring session: junior freezes during incident bridge updates.

choices.text: Maybe you cannot do on-call.
Bridge updates are a skill. Let's script a 3-line template — impact, action, next update time — and rehearse twice this week. I will shadow your next SEV-3.
Throw them into SEV-1 alone.
Take over forever without teaching.

items.explanation: Teach with template, rehearsal, and shadowed practice.

items.scenario: You need to cancel a 1:1 due to an active incident.

choices.text: Skipping.
I need to move our 1:1 — I am on an active SEV-2 bridge. Can we do 20 minutes tomorrow at 10:30, or async bullets today if that is better for you?
No-show without message.
Expect the manager to guess why.

items.scenario: Promotion conversation: report wants a title now; evidence is partial.

choices.text: Sure, whatever.
I support your trajectory. For this cycle, we still need consistent cross-team influence evidence. Here are two gaps and a 90-day plan. If we hit them, I will champion you in the next review.
Never discuss promotions.
Promise a title with no path.

items.explanation: Supportive honesty with gaps and a timeboxed plan.

items.scenario: Skip-level 1:1: engineer says process is slowing delivery.

choices.text: Process is sacred; deal with it.
Thanks for the signal. Which step creates the most delay without reducing risk? I will review it with the leads and we will either streamline it or explain the risk it prevents.
Trash the process publicly same day.
Ignore skip-level feedback.

items.explanation: Seek the costly step, commit to review, keep risk framing.

items.scenario: End a career 1:1 with clear next steps.

choices.text: Talk again someday.
Next steps: you draft the initiative one-pager by Friday; I introduce you to the platform lead next week; we review progress in our 1:1 in two weeks. I will send this summary after the call.
Keep goals only in your head.
Add ten vague aspirations with no owners.

items.explanation: Concrete owners, dates, and a written summary.
